draft.title: Walks, trails, paths and circuits
card: any route along edges from one vertex to another. It may repeat edges and vertices.
a walk that repeats no edge. It may pass through the same vertex more than once.
a walk that repeats no vertex. This means it repeats no edge either.
a circuit is a trail that starts and ends at the same vertex. A cycle is a circuit that repeats no vertex, except the start and end.
draft.remember: Trail: no repeated edge. Path: no repeated vertex. Circuit and cycle: end where they began.

a.q: A route on a graph goes A-B-C-B-D. It uses edges AB, BC, CB and BD, with BC and CB being the same edge. What is the best name for it?
opts: A walk only, as an edge is repeated
A trail, as no vertex is repeated
A path, as it ends at a new vertex
A circuit, as it passes through B twice
a.why: The edge between B and C is used twice, so the route is not a trail or a path. It is a walk only. A circuit needs to end where it began, and this route starts at A and ends at D.
a.clue: Check whether any edge is used twice.

b.q: In a graph, Priya travels P-Q-R-S-Q-T using each edge once only. Which description is correct?
opts: A trail, but not a path
A path, but not a trail
A circuit, as it passes Q twice
A cycle, as no edge is repeated
b.why: No edge is repeated, so it is a trail. Vertex Q is visited twice, so it is not a path. It is not a circuit or cycle, as it starts at P and ends at T. Not repeating an edge does not make it a cycle.
b.clue: Look for a repeated vertex, then check where the route starts and ends.

a.best: A walk only, as an edge is repeated

b.best: A trail, but not a path

check.summary: No problems found. The definitions match the VCE General Mathematics usage, and both questions have exactly one correct option.
